_meta.title: Phase 4 Retrieval Asset Inventory
_meta.purpose: Read-only, complete inventory of every retrieval-related asset in the repo (Phase 4 Step 4), classified as CURRENT / LEGACY / STALE / UNKNOWN against the live production path confirmed in docs/v2/PHASE4_INITIAL_RETRIEVAL_AUDIT.md.

classification_definitions.CURRENT: Actively used by the live production path (retrieval/retriever.py's default retrieve() -> retrieve_hybrid_reranked(), as wired into agent/nodes.py's synthesis_node).
classification_definitions.LEGACY: Superseded by a later, current asset but kept for reference/reproducibility/history (e.g. an intermediate eval config, a raw pre-subsample corpus).
classification_definitions.STALE: Present on disk/in repo but not known to be used by any current path, and possibly outdated relative to CURRENT config (e.g. experimental index variants).
classification_definitions.UNKNOWN: Cannot be determined from available evidence without guessing; stated explicitly rather than assumed.

_meta.note_on_historical_docs: Root-level PHASE3_*.md / RESULTS_RAG_COMPARISON.md / CITATIONS_BUG_INVESTIGATION.md / EVAL_HANG_FIX_COMPLETE.md / CHEMBL_BACKFILL_COMPLETE.md predate this project's current V2 phase-gate numbering. Their 'Phase 3' label is NOT this project's Phase 3 (already complete, unrelated). Their factual build/experiment history is used here; their metric numbers are flagged HISTORICAL/UNVERIFIED and are not treated as current baselines.

corpus_assets.description: Production PubMed abstract corpus actually loaded by the index-build pipeline and, transitively, by the live data/index/ files. One JSON record per line: pmid, title, abstract, journal, pub_date, year, doi, url, query.
corpus_assets.produced_by: Deterministic subsample (random.seed(42)) of data/corpus/abstracts_raw_all.jsonl, per retrieval/README.md's 'Known gap' section and PHASE3_RETRIEVAL_LAYER_COMPLETE.md section 1. NOT reproducible from any committed script (see integrity_issues_found).
corpus_assets.classification_rationale: This is the corpus data/index/{faiss.index,bm25.pkl,chunks.jsonl,index_meta.json} was built from (index_meta.json num_abstracts=9000 matches exactly); that index is what retrieval/retriever.py loads by default and what agent/nodes.py's synthesis_node calls via retrieve().

corpus_assets.description: Full raw fetch of unique PubMed abstracts across all 72 hardcoded query terms in retrieval/build_corpus.py, before the 9,000-record subsample was taken. Kept for reference per retrieval/README.md.
corpus_assets.produced_by: retrieval/build_corpus.py::fetch_corpus() (reproducible from committed code, modulo PubMed's live index changing over time).
corpus_assets.classification_rationale: Superseded input to the CURRENT corpus (abstracts.jsonl); not itself loaded by any index-build default path or by retrieval/retriever.py. Kept for reproducibility/reference of the pre-subsample state, and as the only remaining evidence of what the subsample step operated on.

main.classification_rationale: retrieval/retriever.py's default INDEX_PATH/CHUNKS_PATH/BM25_PATH constants point here with no variant subdirectory; this is what agent/nodes.py's synthesis_node retrieves against via retrieve() -> retrieve_hybrid_reranked(). Confirmed directly in docs/v2/PHASE4_INITIAL_RETRIEVAL_AUDIT.md section A.

chunk_abstract(): fixed word-count windows (180 words / 30-word overlap default) since PubMed abstracts have no reliable paragraph structure to split on.

Imported directly by agent/nodes.py.

integrity_issues_found.title: Production corpus (13,115 -> 9,000 abstracts) subsampling step has no committed script
integrity_issues_found.description: The live/CURRENT corpus data/corpus/abstracts.jsonl (9,000 records, what data/index/ was built from and what agent/nodes.py retrieves against) was produced by deterministically subsampling (random.seed(42)) the raw 13,115-abstract fetch preserved at data/corpus/abstracts_raw_all.jsonl. retrieval/build_corpus.py as committed today writes every fetched record straight through with no subsampling step at all, and git log --follow on that file shows only one commit ever touched it (the current version). The subsample was done via an ad hoc, uncommitted script at build time and cannot be reproduced from anything currently checked in.
integrity_issues_found.relevant_directive: Governing Phase 4 directive Step 28: 'Index builds must be reproducible... do not rely on opaque manually generated index files.'
integrity_issues_found.impact: A fresh clone + a fresh `python -m retrieval.build_corpus` run today CANNOT regenerate the exact corpus currently backing production retrieval -- only an equivalent-ish 13,115-abstract raw fetch (itself subject to PubMed's live index drift over time). The actually-running data/ artifacts are gitignored and were copied in from a prior build, not regenerated by any committed pipeline end-to-end.

integrity_issues_found.title: All of data/ (corpus + index + variants, ~406MB) is gitignored -- nothing under data/ arrives via git clone or git merge
integrity_issues_found.description: repo-root .gitignore excludes data/ entirely. Every corpus/index asset cataloged above physically exists only on this local disk (or wherever it was last copied from -- see PHASE3_WIRING_COMPLETE.md's note that data/ was copied from a sibling worktree during the original wiring pass). A fresh clone of this repository has none of retrieval/'s corpus/index files and cannot serve RAG-backed synthesis until someone manually rebuilds or copies data/ in.
integrity_issues_found.impact: Combined with the corpus-subsample gap above, a from-scratch rebuild today produces a corpus that is neither byte-identical to production NOR obtainable any other reproducible way.

integrity_issues_found.title: No automated test coverage exists for the RAG retrieval layer
integrity_issues_found.description: tests/test_nodes.py exercises agent/nodes.py broadly but does not call _retrieve_rag_context, _dedupe_retrieved_by_pmid, or _format_retrieved_context; no test file under tests/ references faiss, BM25, CrossEncoder, or retrieve(). This is a live, production-wired code path with zero test coverage, unlike the rest of the codebase's tested surfaces (pubmed/clinical_trials/chembl tools, orchestration, NLU).
integrity_issues_found.impact: Regressions in RAG retrieval wiring (dedup, context formatting, the RAG-vs-API citation-provenance distinction) would not be caught by the existing test suite.

integrity_issues_found.title: All eval_results_*.json Recall@10 numbers are historical, LLM-judge-labeled, and not independently re-verified
integrity_issues_found.description: Every metric in every eval_results_*.json / eval_set*.json file comes from LLM-assisted relevance labeling (judge_model=nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b) explicitly described in each eval-set's own 'methodology' field as 'NOT human-verified.' Per the governing Phase 4 directive, these should not be treated as current ground truth without re-running retrieval/measure_recall.py.
integrity_issues_found.impact: Any Phase 4 claim about current retrieval quality needs an independent re-run, not a citation of these files.

integrity_issues_found.title: Several grounding eval_results_*.json files have null mode/variant/expand fields
integrity_issues_found.description: eval_results_grounding_bge_dense.json, eval_results_grounding_bge_hybrid.json, eval_results_grounding_bm25_weight_2x.json, eval_results_grounding_bm25_weight_3x.json, eval_results_grounding_hyde_dense_only.json, and eval_results_grounding_hyde_hybrid.json all have mode/variant/expand recorded as null/None in the JSON itself -- what technique each represents has to be inferred from the filename and cross-referenced against git log commit messages (2e1e659, 7479a1d, bcae012), not read directly out of the result file's own structured fields.
evidence: Direct inspection of the six files' 'mode'/'variant'/'expand' keys
integrity_issues_found.impact: Lower-severity documentation/provenance gap: these result files are less self-describing than the earlier eval_results_*.json files (baseline/hybrid/bge_base_*/chunk_*/expansion_hybrid), which do populate these fields.

integrity_issues_found.title: requirements.txt labels the retrieval dependency block '# RAG / retrieval layer (Phase 3)', colliding with this project's current V2 Phase 3 (unrelated, already complete)
integrity_issues_found.description: Could cause a future contributor scoping V2 Phase 4 work to wrongly assume the retrieval layer was already covered/frozen under V2's Phase 3 tool-orchestration gate and skip auditing it.
integrity_issues_found.impact: Documentation/naming hazard only, no functional impact.
